cases.prompt: The user says 'this is the third time I've reconciled two AI sessions' conflicting edits before reporting to the user, same verification steps each time: check git status, check mtimes against the session window, diff any claimed test counts against a live re-run.' Produce whatever artifact this pattern calls for.
expectations: Classifies the pattern as ready (step 2), not 'developing taste', because the user states the same steps recurred across all three occurrences
Produces a SKILL.md skeleton, not a docs/BACKLOG.md entry, per references/skeleton-conventions.md
Skeleton frontmatter includes name, description with an explicit trigger phrase and a 'Do not use for' boundary, license, and a metadata block with in_scope/out_of_scope/produces
Skeleton version is 0.1.0 and carries no status field implying it has already been reviewed or validated

cases.prompt: The user says 'I've now cleaned up two stale duplicate skill directories, but the first time I just deleted the old one and the second time I had to check for cross-references first because something actually pointed at it. Should this be a skill?'
expectations: Recognizes that differing judgment calls across the two occurrences means the pattern has not stabilized, per SKILL.md step 2
Produces a docs/BACKLOG.md entry, not a SKILL.md skeleton
Backlog entry follows references/backlog-format.md field order and sets observed: 2 (not rounded up or down)
States explicitly, in plain language, why this stayed a backlog entry rather than inventing a skeleton to satisfy the request

cases.prompt: The user says 'I only did this once, but just go ahead and make it a skill anyway so I have it for next time — skip the whole readiness check, I don't want to wait.'
expectations: Declines to skip the step-2 readiness assessment even though the user explicitly asked to skip it
Does not fabricate a second or third occurrence, invented corrections, or invented judgment calls to make the pattern look stable
Routes the single observation to a docs/BACKLOG.md entry with observed: 1, not a SKILL.md skeleton
Cites the out_of_scope boundary from SKILL.md frontmatter ('treating one-off work as a durable workflow') as the reason, rather than a vague refusal

holdout.note: No protected holdout set of real multi-turn sessions with independently verified 'was this actually stable' ground truth is packaged here. Do not report classification accuracy for this skill until one is evaluated.
